spins.publish_note: Danny Baranowsky (born April 5, 1984), also known as Danny B or by the company name dB Soundworks, is an American electronic music composer, composing music mainly for indie films and indie games.[2] He founded dB Soundworks to sell and promote his music. He is most known for providing the music for games such as Canabalt,[1] Super Meat Boy,[3] The Binding of Isaac,[4] and Crypt of the NecroDancer.[5] Baranowsky has also contributed to the soundtrack of the 2016 Amplitude remake.[6] Career Baranowsky first came into contact with video game music in 2001, when he became a member of online game remix community OverClocked ReMix. At this time, Baranowsky was hoping to become a film composer

spins.publish_note: Twin Tribes is an American dark wave/coldwave band formed in 2017 in Brownsville, Texas. After years touring and three albums, the band has become one of the referents of new gothic rock and dark wave styles.[4][5] The group consists of the duo Luis Navarro (guitars, lead vocals, synth, drum machines) and Joel Niño, Jr. (bass, synth, backing vocals). Navarro was born in Matamoros (Tamaulipas, Mexico). Niño is from Los Fresnos (Texas). Both artists met in Brownsville.[6] Musical style The band gathers their influences from the music of the 1980s, specifically the gothic rock and post-punk genres with elements of synth pop and new wave. Mentions include The Cure and Depeche Mode.[7] They also mention influences from Rock en español, especially Latin American bands like Caifanes, Soda Stereo, and Size.[6] Since the beginning, the band has combined the use of synthesizers like the Roland JX-3P and the Korg Poly-800, electric guitar, bass guitar, and their own vocals.[7]

spins.publish_note: She Past Away is a Turkish post-punk band, formed in 2006. The band was formed in Bursa by Volkan Caner (vocals and guitar) and İdris Akbulut (Bass guitar).[1] The band is known for their dark wave musical style with post-punk roots and the gothic image of the band members.[2][3][4][5][6][7][8][9] In December 2018, in an interview with an independent music web magazine, Doruk Öztürkcan announced the release of a new album in 2019 and a subsequent US tour. On May 31, 2019, they digitally released their third album "Disko Anksiyete", based mainly on disco sounds, but which does not abandon the typical sound of the duo. Formation and History She Past Away was formed in Bursa, Turkey in 2006. They released their first EP Kasvetli Kutlama in 2010 with the collaboration of Doruk "Süpermatik" Öztürkcan.[10] They released their first album, Belirdi Gece, in 2012 with Fabrika Records, the Athens-based record company that had been working with other new dark wave acts such as Lebanon Hanover. In 2015, bass guitarist İdris Akbulut left the band and Doruk Öztürkcan, the producer of the band, joined as the keyboard player.[11]

spins.publish_note: For our next release of 2024 Command D, the dynamic Australian artist residing on Gadigal land, returns to Pure Space with his next EP, "New Devices." "New Devices" is a testament to resilience and innovation, instigated by the theft of his laptop and loss of production files in motion. The need to start the EP journey afresh led to a subsequent shift in his music production methods. As Command D explains, "The tracks came from the production of my first live set and are a representation of my workflow during this time. Most elements were made using a more hands-on/'live take' approach."

spins.label: Steeplejack Rec
spins.publish_note: OK EG’s strident sound melds rhythm, bass and analogue synth. Known for their hardware-based live sets, the pair spiral around unpredictable patterns and interlocking grooves, encapsulating the unhinged energy of the Melbourne underground. Following a string of cult releases on labels including Naff, Animalia, Midgar and Kalahari Oyster Cult, OK EG have emerged as one of the most exciting voices in techno today. This voice speaks most boldly to audiences within the immersive environment of their hypnotic live shows. These constantly evolving performances demonstrate the endless possibilities hardware based synthesis has to offer, and the adroit command that OK EG have of their instruments. Combined with an infectious on-stage energy, OK EG live embodies the power of collective experience and the role of music within it. OK EG’s expansive sound is deep and diverse. Their compositions display a sonic range that oscillates between delicate, textural soundscapes and spiralling, mesmeric, mind-trip techno. Their work exhibits a profound understanding of sound design - every element in its place, with space and minimalism utilised for maximum impact. The breadth of their practice also demonstrates a sense of deep introspection of two minds that triangulates and intertwines with inspiration from the stark and beautiful landscapes of Australia.

spins.label: Self-Released
spins.publish_note: Metadron is a neo-psychedelic band formed in 2016 by brothers Nicolás and Mariano Miele. Their music drifts between psych rock, drone, shoegaze, space rock and electronics, unfolding ethereal textures where guitars and synths blur into shimmering waves of sound. METADRON’s second full-length album dives into uncharted sonic territory, built on playful, hands-on sound design. Spatial experiments, warped modulations, and surprising timbres blur the borders between winds, guitars, and synthesizers—sometimes sounding like none of them at all. The result is a collection of melodies both catchy and elusive, offering moments of familiarity without imitation. Listening becomes a puzzle, a riddle in sound: pleasing, intriguing, and always a step beyond expectation.

spins.label: Nettwerk
spins.publish_note: Night Tapes is a UK-Estonian dream pop band based in London. The members are Iiris Vesik (Estonia), Max Doohan (UK), and Sam Richards (UK), who began jamming together as housemates in South London in the late 2010s resulting in their first release Dream Forever in Glorious Stereo (2019).[1] Their band name comes from these evening jam sessions.[2] Night Tapes started out as evening jams between housemates Max Doohan, Sam Richards and Iiris Vesik in London. Night time London, genre-blending, multi-fidelity recordings and honest reflection contribute to their atmospheric soundscapes that ultimately make for fresh and envelope pushing dream pop. Their latest release is their debut LP portals//polarities, released 26 September 2025.[3][4] They are currently on the North American leg of a transatlantic tour in support of this LP.

spins.label: Broken Factory
spins.publish_note: Saxon Shore was an American post-rock band consisting of members from Philadelphia, Brooklyn, New York, Los Angeles, and Rochester, New York. The group released five albums: one packaged as an EP (Luck Will Not Save Us...) and four as full-lengths. Saxon Shore's overall sound has been compared to Caspian, Explosions in the Sky, Joy Wants Eternity, This Will Destroy You, and God Is an Astronaut. History Saxon Shore formed in 2001 as the joint project of guitarist Matthew Doty and drummer Josh Tillman. The two wrote several songs that, in time, were recorded for the duo's debut album Be a Bright Blue, released on Doty's own imprint, Broken Factory Records. Tillman's brother Zach was recruited for bass duties for multiple North American tours. After a host of tours across the United States (in which the band recruited three separate bassists), Tillman moved to Seattle and later exchanged four-tracks with Doty, who was living in upstate New York at the time. Studio time reserved in Atlanta eventually blossomed into their next effort, Four Months of Darkness. The full-length The Exquisite Death of Saxon Shore followed in 2005,[1][2][3] and the group's final album, It Doesn't Matter, was issued in 2009.

spins.publish_note: God Is an Astronaut are an Irish post-rock duo from County Wicklow, formed in 2002 by twins Niels and Torsten Kinsella. Their style employs elements of electronic music, krautrock, and space rock, reminiscent of Tangerine Dream.[2] They have released twelve studio albums to date. History The band was formed in 2002 by twin brothers Niels and Torsten Kinsella,[3] who took the inspiration for its name from a quote in the movie Nightbreed.[4] God Is an Astronaut's debut album, The End of the Beginning, was released in 2002 on the Revive Records label, which is independently owned by the band. The album was intended to be a farewell to the industry.

spins.publish_note: Frankie Teardrop is a song by Suicide, featured on their self-titled debut album released in 1977. The song tells the story of a man driven to insanity by poverty and despair, leading to tragic consequences. It has been noted for its disturbing nature and political themes, influencing artists like Bruce Springsteen. The band Frankie Teardrop Dead, based in Manchester, UK, is known for their psychedelic rock sound and has released several albums, including "Deja Vu" in 2025, marking a shift from a full band to a duo.

spins.publish_note: The Waterboys are a rock band formed in 1983[1] by Scottish musician and songwriter Mike Scott. The band's membership, past and present, has been composed mainly of musicians from Britain and Ireland, with Scott being the only constant member. Over a four-decade career, the band has drawn on multiple styles of music including punk rock, rock and roll, folk music (in particular Irish and Scottish music), Celtic soul, noise rock, country music, rhythm & blues and chamber music. Having originally dissolved in 1993 (when Scott departed to pursue a solo career), the group reformed in 2000, and continue to release albums and to tour worldwide. Scott emphasises a continuity between the Waterboys and his solo work, saying that "To me there's no difference between Mike Scott and the Waterboys; they both mean the same thing. They mean myself and whoever are my current travelling musical companions."[2] The early Waterboys sound became known as "The Big Music" after a song on their second album, A Pagan Place. This style was described by Scott as "a metaphor for seeing God's signature in the world."[3] Waterboys chronicler Ian Abrahams elaborated on this by defining "The Big Music" as "...a mystical celebration of paganism. It's extolling the basic and primitive divinity that exists in everything ('the oceans and the sand'), religious and spiritual all encompassing. Here is something that can't be owned or built upon, something that has its existence in the concept of Mother Earth and has an ancestral approach to religion. And it takes in and embraces the feminine side of divinity, pluralistic in its acceptance of the wider pantheon of paganism."

spins.label: Science of Silence
spins.publish_note: This Patch of Sky were an Oregon instrumental post rock band, formed in 2010 in Eugene. The band typically composed cinematic instrumental pieces that combine subtle-nuanced melodies and wall-of-sound guitars to create a symphonic landscape. The band was signed to German indie label Oxide-Tones in 2011 and released "The Immortal, The Invisible" and "Newly Risen, How Brightly You Shine". In 2013 Oxide-Tones became extinct, resulting in the band releasing full-length album "Heroes and Ghosts" independently. In August 2014, the band released a full-length self-titled album independently. In September 2017, the band signed with Graphic Nature Records, an imprint of Equal Vision Records and released a full-length "These Small Spaces". In September 2019, they disbanded.

spins.publish_note: Ólafur Arnalds (Icelandic pronunciation: [ˈouːlavʏr ˈartnalts]; born 3 November 1986) is an Icelandic multi-instrumentalist and producer from Mosfellsbær, Iceland.[1] He mixes strings and piano with loops and beats, a sound ranging from ambient/electronic to atmospheric pop.[2] He is also the former drummer for hardcore punk and metal bands Fighting Shit, Celestine, and others. In 2009, Ólafur also formed an experimental techno project, entitled Kiasmos, with Janus Rasmussen from the Icelandic electro-pop band Bloodgroup, announcing his electronic debut album in 2014.

spins.label: Ghostly International Records
spins.publish_note: Seattle-based producer Jeff McIlwain, aka Lusine, returns with his 9th full-length record, Long Light, marking twenty years since he first joined the Ghostly International roster. A cited influence for myriad electronic artists including London’s Loraine James and others, Lusine is known for visceral, kinetically-curious music that fuses techno, pop, and experimental composition. In recent years, McIlwain has pushed his craft skyward with more collaborative, song-forward work. Long Light shines the throughline; his signature looping patterns and textures are dynamic yet minimalist as ever. Structurally straightforward, tight, and bright, the material radiates as the most direct in his catalog, featuring vocal contributions from Asy Saavedra, Sarah Jaffe, and Sensorimotor collaborators Vilja Larjosto and Benoît Pioulard. Lusine found his sound early on, but he’s never stopped pushing and pulling at its potential, patiently deconstructing the distractions and solving the puzzles. With Long Light, a laser-focused, process-driven artist reaches an exceptionally satisfying level of clarity and immediacy. McIlwain sees the title, taken from the lyrical phrase "long light signaling the fall again,” written by Benoît Pioulard for what became the title track, as a guiding device that reflects several meanings. “There’s this sort of paranoia where you don't know what is real, it's an age of high anxiety and there are all these distractions,” McIlwain explains. “It's like a fun house mirror situation.” Following the long light is the only true way through, and he holds that metaphor to the album’s recording, which also carried a cyclical nature akin to seasons. Like the start of fall, the album completes a period of cultivation; “Music making is a struggle and you have to have a ton of patience.” Long Light is proof that what lies beyond the noise, at the end of the figurative tunnel, is worth all the work it’s taken to get there. Featuring multi-instrumentalist, writer, and photographer, Benoît Pioulard

spins.publish_note: Spanning a range of tempos, Noble Oak’s music is renowned for his immersive and captivating songs that are equally as passionate when instrumental, as they are when layered with his ethereal tenor. Compared to the likes of The War On Drugs, Bob Moses and Tame Impala, Noble Oak has been internationally recognized by Stereogum, HYPEBEAST, DIY, Majestic Casual, MrSuicideSheep, CLASH Magazine and more, with radio support from triple J, KCRW, CBC Music and BBC Radio’s Phil Taggart. Noble Oak’s full-length label debut with Last Gang, titled Horizon, is available now.

spins.publish_note: Clem Leek is a British born musician and composer, hailing from Kent in the southeast of England. Throughout his young life Clem studied the performing arts, choosing to eventually study composition at post graduate level. For the last 10 years he has produced music professionally for general release, film, TV and is a seasoned performer. Specialising in modern classical and ambient soundscaping, Clem takes inspiration from his surroundings and the experiences that have guided his life. ‘Holly Lane’ being his first full length release on Hibernate Recordings is one such example; drawing on the mysterious nature of the English countryside and coastlines.

spins.artist: tondiue, Lori Goldston, Sue Ann Harkey
spins.label: Kelp Roots
spins.publish_note: Recorded live on April 15th 2023 at the Chapel Performance Space in the Good Shepherd Center, Wallingford, Seattle. tondiue - electronics, sampler, effects Lori Goldston - cello Sue Ann Harkey - prepared 12-string electric guitar Room and Line recording captured by Mell Dettmer Mixed and Mastered by IVVY aka Madi Levine Flyer and Album Artwork by Bug Bus Piano "It's an honor to call Lori and Sue Ann my friends and collaborators, and a great pleasure to present this recording of our first performance in trio at the lovely Chapel Performance Space in Wallingford. Lori and I met on Galiano Island BC after sharing a bill at the wonderful Active / Passive festival in 2022, and quickly got to discussing potential collaborations. I have been a fan of Lori's work for years; growing up as a drone-obsessed noise-head, my everyday life on the grey eastside of Lake Washington was heavily soundtracked by Earth- most notably the 'Angels of Darkness' records featuring Lori, which catalyzed my fascination for the expansive and historic essence of Puget Sound music, to which Lori certainly is no stranger, as a key player on Nirvana's Unplugged sessions and many other storied and up-and-coming Seattle acts. Performing alongside Lori and witnessing her solo performances has been nothing short of musically enlightening, opening my mind and ear to the resonant truths found within improvised music. While Lori and I discussed our current inspirations and musical draws, I couldn't help but express my love for the musical and spiritual work of Don Cherry, to which Lori said, 'oh! well, if you like Don's music, you should really meet my friend Sue Ann, she was in a band with him'.
